findings.finding: the group holds a THIRD non-household sheet, and it is the one that names the wards. Thirty numbered enumerating pages, each with its own free-white age-band totals, braced into First through Sixth Ward, with ward subtotal rules and a grand total. findings.why_it_matters: the README already records two non-household sheets - printed 206, the certificate, and printed 237, 'the other recapitulation', whose THIRTY ruled lines carry division totals gathered into SIX blocks summing to 4,466 against the 4,470 written at its foot. This sheet has the SAME shape - thirty rows, six groups - but broken out by age band and with the six groups NAMED as the city's wards. So it is a second, independent statement of the same recapitulation: it can be added against 237's division totals, it may bear on the residual of 4 that 237 leaves open, and it attributes every one of the thirty enumerating pages to a ward. Thirty pages at the ~31 ruled lines these sheets carry is about 930 households against the 964 the IPUMS extract holds, so it is also a completeness test for the whole reading programme. NONE of that is done here: this pass records that the sheet exists and what it is.
